voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 51–53: the members of the assembly urge Janamejaya to grant the brahmin his boon; he grants it: the sacrifice ends, Takshaka lives, and the words of the builder (the suta who foretold that a brahmin would stop the rite, 1.47) come true. The king honours the priests and the assembly and the builder; Astika, having done what he came to do, returns home. The serpents, overjoyed, offer him a boon; he asks that whoever recites this story of his, morning or evening, with a calm mind, shall have nothing to fear from serpents; they grant it. Sauti adds that in the intervals of that sacrifice Vaishampayana, Vyasa's disciple, told the Mahabharata to Janamejaya (1.53). (The cliffhanger turns to the next arc: Shaunaka asks for the story of his own family, the Bhrigus, 1.4–5, reordered.)
structure: From episode 21: COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, ≤ 3 s; opening chosen by content (not a fixed rotation): a statement card over the fire sinking; the ARC FINALE: a ≥ 4 s lit payoff close-up of Astika, then the arc-end card (episodes 31–40, the playlist) before the cliffhanger and the short Next) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band over its first shot → turn at 40–60 % after one ≈ 0.9 s rest → the cliffhanger image + line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band over the cliffhanger image that dissolves into frame 1. Gate: tools/gate.mjs (run by tools/render.mjs).

strings.recapLine: Takshaka hung in the air. Would the king keep his word?
strings.arcPlaylist: The whole arc is in the Astika playlist

lines.text: A king's word put out the fire.
lines.say: A king's word [p:40] put out the fire.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a statement card over the image): the great fire of the snake sacrifice sinking from frame 1, the serpent held above it in gold rings; the card in the smoke above.

lines.text: The whole assembly urged the king: give the boy his boon.
lines.say: The whole assembly urged the king: [p:150] give the boy his boon.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): the seated kings and sages of the assembly turn to Janamejaya, hands raised; the fire roars behind.

lines.speaker: janamejaya
lines.text: "So be it. Let the sacrifice end. Let Takshaka live."
lines.say: So be it. [p:250] Let the sacrifice end. [p:250] Let Takshaka live.
lines.note: STORY 1 (Janamejaya speaks): the king lowers his raised arm, lit gold, the fire off to the side; his face eases.

lines.text: And the great fire sank into embers.
lines.say: And the great fire [p:80] sank into embers.
lines.note: STORY 2: NEW LIGHT, the enclosure after the fire: the flames drop to a bed of embers; grey smoke thins; a cool blue dusk comes down over the posts.

lines.text: The builder's warning had come true: a brahmin had stopped the rite.
lines.say: The builder's warning had come true: [p:150] a brahmin had stopped the rite.
lines.note: STORY 3: the old builder (episode 8's sthapati) nods at the edge of the enclosure, his measuring cord in hand; plaque "The builder's warning · episode 8".

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: The serpents were saved by a boy who was half serpent.
lines.say: The serpents were saved [p:80] by a boy who was half serpent.
lines.note: FRAME (Sauti, a twenty-eighth angle: the last of the arc: frontal, level, the fire low between him and us; the elder and the sages lit warm around him).

lines.text: Then the serpents came to Astika, overjoyed, and offered him a boon.
lines.say: Then the serpents came to Astika, [p:100] overjoyed, [p:100] and offered him a boon.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %): after the 0.9 s silence: NEW LIGHT, Vasuki's hall at dawn in full gold (the hall's brightest light): the serpents rise in rings around the boy, Vasuki and Elapatra among them, every head bowed.

lines.speaker: astika
lines.text: "Whoever tells this story, let them never fear a serpent."
lines.say: Whoever tells this story, [p:150] let them never fear a serpent.
lines.note: STORY 5 (Astika speaks): the boy, lit gold, his hand open toward the serpents. The serpents' hoods all lift together on "serpent": the boon is granted.

lines.text: And Astika went home, to his mother.
lines.say: And Astika went home, [p:150] to his mother.
lines.note: STORY 7 · THE ARC'S PAYOFF (≥ 4 s, lit, close): the mother kneels and the boy runs into her arms in the gold hall; Vasuki's hood over them both; a slow push in on their faces, held through the long post.

lines.text: And in the pauses of that sacrifice, the Mahabharata was told.
lines.say: And in the pauses of that sacrifice, [p:120] the Mahabharata was told.
lines.note: STORY 8: the enclosure at night, the embers low; beside them Vaishampayana begins to speak to the seated king (episode 4's disciple), palm leaves open.

lines.text: The end of an arc · Astika
lines.note: The ARC-END CARD (silent): over the told shot, a lapis cartouche: THE END OF AN ARC · ASTIKA · Episodes 31–40 · the whole arc is in the Astika playlist.

lines.text: But Sauti had another family to speak of: Shaunaka's own.
lines.say: But Sauti had another family to speak of: [p:250] Shaunaka's own.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (cliffhanger, the catalog line): back at the Naimisha fire: Sauti turns to the elder; behind the elder, in the fire's smoke, the faint shape of a woman and a boar (the next arc).

lines.text: Next: The Bride and the Demon
lines.note: The arc's serpent cartouche (its last time) over the cliffhanger image; dissolve into frame 1.
